tools.name: signl4_list_teams
tools.description: List the SIGNL4 teams the API key can access: id, name, description, time zone and member ids. Team ids are needed to raise alerts and to look up categories and duties. GET /v3/teams.

tools.name: signl4_get_team
tools.description: One SIGNL4 team: name, description, time zone, member ids. GET /v3/teams/{teamId}.

tools.name: signl4_list_users
tools.description: List the SIGNL4 users the key can access with name, e-mail, contact addresses, activation state and duty status per team (dutyMode, onDutyTime). User ids are needed to acknowledge/close/annotate alerts. GET /v3/users.

tools.name: signl4_get_user
tools.description: One SIGNL4 user: name, e-mail, contact addresses, time zone and duty status per team. GET /v3/users/{userId}.

tools.name: signl4_list_team_users
tools.description: List the users of the given teams (all accessible teams by default) with duty status. Teams that cannot be read are reported under `errors`. GET /v3/teams/users.

tools.name: signl4_list_categories
tools.description: List the alert categories of a team (name, color, keywords used to auto-classify alerts). The category name can be passed to signl4_raise_alert. GET /v3/categories/{teamId}.

tools.name: signl4_list_alerts
tools.description: Search SIGNL4 alerts (signls), newest first, with status, severity, category and history (created, acknowledged, closed). Filter by team, status, creation time, text or external id. Up to 100 per page; pass the returned continuation_token to get the next page. POST /v3/signls/paged (a read).

tools.name: signl4_get_alert
tools.description: Full detail of one alert: title, text, severity, category, status and delivery status, history (who acknowledged/closed it and when), parameters, attachments and escalations with per-user delivery. GET /v3/signls/{signlId}/details.

tools.name: signl4_get_alert_timeline
tools.description: The ordered timeline of an alert: creation, notifications, acknowledgements, annotations, escalations and remote actions. GET /v3/signls/{signlId}/timeline.

tools.name: signl4_get_alert_report
tools.description: Alert volume and response statistics per team over several time periods: acknowledged, closed and unhandled counts, overall and per category (optionally for one user). Teams that cannot be read are reported under `errors`. GET /v3/signls/report.

tools.name: signl4_raise_alert
tools.description: WRITE: raise a new alert in a SIGNL4 team. THIS NOTIFIES REAL PEOPLE: every team member currently on duty is paged (push, SMS and/or voice call according to their settings) and the alert escalates if nobody acknowledges it. Only use it when the user clearly asked to alert the team; never for tests u

tools.name: signl4_acknowledge_alert
tools.description: WRITE: acknowledge an alert on behalf of a SIGNL4 user (recorded in its history under that user). Stops escalation to further tiers for that alert. POST /v3/signls/{signlId}/acknowledge.

tools.name: signl4_close_alert
tools.description: WRITE: close (resolve) an alert on behalf of a SIGNL4 user; it leaves the open list and stops all further notifications. POST /v3/signls/{signlId}/close.

tools.name: signl4_annotate_alert
tools.description: WRITE: add a text note to an alert's timeline on behalf of a SIGNL4 user. The note is visible to the team in the app. It does not page anyone by itself. POST /v3/signls/{signlId}/annotate.

tools.name: signl4_list_duty_schedules
tools.description: Planned on-call duty schedules (who is on duty when): start/end, team, user, tier, stand-in and shift info. Filter by team, user and time window. POST /v3/schedules (a read).

tools.name: signl4_get_duty_status
tools.description: Whether a user is currently on or off duty in each of their teams (dutyMode, onDutyTime, tier). GET /v3/users/{userId}/dutyStatus.

tools.name: signl4_get_duty_summary
tools.description: Duty assistant info per team: whether it is enabled and the last two (or all) duty periods. GET /v3/duties/summary.

tools.name: signl4_list_audit_logs
tools.description: Audit log of changes and events in the SIGNL4 subscription (who changed what, when). Filter by team, time window and message text; pass the returned continuation_token for the next page. GET /v3/audits.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: signl4_list_alerts, signl4_get_alert_timeline, signl4_close_alert, signl4_list_duty_schedules, signl4_list_audit_logs · Private data: signl4_list_teams, signl4_list_users, signl4_get_user · Public sink: signl4_list_alerts, signl4_raise_alert, signl4_acknowledge_alert, signl4_close_alert, signl4_annotate_alert, signl4_list_duty_schedules.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: signl4_list_alerts, signl4_get_alert_timeline, signl4_close_alert, signl4_list_duty_schedules, signl4_list_audit_logs · Private data: signl4_list_teams, signl4_list_users, signl4_get_user · Public sink: signl4_list_alerts, signl4_raise_alert, signl4_acknowledge_alert, signl4_close_alert, signl4_annotate_alert, signl4_list_duty_schedules

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
